item.content:encoded:
Man, why is it that all my favorite stories had to stop in 2014? first MTF Theta-90, now this!

Regardless, this is one of my favorite tales on the site. It perfectly captures the whimsy of Wondertainment stuff while not shying away from the grimdarkness of a lot of other foundation stuff; it reminds me a lot of the anime "The Irresponsible Captain Tyler", which is more or less about a comedy character blundering his way through a hyper-serious space opera. Isabel feels much the same; she's out of place, but she's supposed to be, and it reads great. +1

item.content:encoded:
The thing to remember is that you can't sever Wondertainment from humanity. Wondertainment is not a force outside of humanity, but an emanation and manifestation of it.

For ease of use, yes, the first Wondertainment invented fire. There were those before that particular time, though - The true beginning of Wondertainment came with the dawn of human sapience. But fire's a good shorthand for the lineage.

The old man with the wolf is a neanderthal incarnation of Wondertainment, based mostly on this reconstruction.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Just read through all the current ADVENTURES IN CAPITALISM so far, and I am loving it. I was personally a little put-off at the idea of Dr. Wondertainment being a person (violates my Headcannon), but I was prepared to not hold that against you. And then I found myself loving your interpretation. And now she's not a person! I'm loving the implication that Wondertainment is a meta-existence, completely reinventing itself on and on down the years, a force for creation and wonder, the manifestation of human imagination that's been with us since we were cave men. (The first Dr. Wondertainment invented fire? Did I read that right?)

I went into this determined to treat it fairly despite my own headcannon. It has now replaced my headcannon. +1 forever and ever. Amen.

(Also that old man with the wolf that saved her was Odin, right? Because if the Dresden Files has taught me anything it's that the Santa myth has its origins in Badass Norse Deities.)
